costGuide.title: Land Rover 306D1 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 306D1 typically takes 15-20 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a 306D1 engine replacement is the condition of the crankshaft bearings and the oil pump assembly. Units with documented recent bearing replacements and flushed oil coolers command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a complex twin-turbo V6, a full 306D1 rebuild is considerably more expensive than naturally aspirated alternatives. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Land Rover 306D1 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Crankshaft Bearing Failure (Tin-Aluminium Coating Fatigue)
items.whatHappens: The tin-aluminium coating on the crankshaft bearings is prone to fatigue and flaking. This leads to spun bearings, sudden loss of oil pressure, and catastrophic bottom-end failure, often preceded by a distinct cold-start knock.
items.repairVsReplace: This failure typically writes off the engine. A full 306D1 engine replacement or a comprehensive bottom-end rebuild is the only viable solution once bearing damage has occurred.

items.title: Oil Pump and Turbo Contamination
items.whatHappens: Debris from failing bearings or inherent oil pump wear circulates through the system, contaminating the turbochargers and restricting oil galleries.
items.repairVsReplace: Requires a full engine strip, oil cooler flush, and turbo replacement. If caught too late, metal debris in the sump mandates a full 306D1 engine replacement to prevent immediate recurrence.

items.title: EGR and DPF Clogging (Urban Use)
items.whatHappens: Restricted exhaust flow from clogged EGR valves or DPFs increases backpressure, exacerbating oil dilution and accelerating bearing wear.
items.repairVsReplace: Cleaning or replacing the EGR and DPF is a standard repair, but it acts as a critical preventative measure to protect the vulnerable bottom end of the 306D1.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2014 updates saw minor revisions to the oil pump drive chains, but the fundamental tin-aluminium bearing vulnerability remains a documented pattern across the 306D1 lifespan .
failures.cta: Compare rebuilt 306D1 prices with the failure already addressed

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 306D1
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible on the passenger side near the oil filter housing, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The 306D1 is frequently confused with the earlier Land Rover 276DT (which lacks the twin-turbo setup and has a different oil pump design) or the later Land Rover 30DDTX. Fitting a 276DT or 30DDTX into a 306D1 vehicle requires different ECU mapping, turbo plumbing, and engine mounts, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

relatives.description: - the 2.7L TDV6 it replaced, which suffered from oil pump housing failures but lacked the specific tin-aluminium bearing fatigue seen in the 3.0L units.
- the 2016+ update that introduced revised bearing materials and improved oil pump drive chains to mitigate the catastrophic bottom-end failure risk.
- the broader 3.0L SDV6/TDV6 family code that shares the exact same architecture, failure patterns, and replacement procedures as the 306D1.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 306D1 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 306D1 is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof of recent crankshaft bearing inspection/replacement and oil pump servicing. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a ticking time bomb is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used 306D1 engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 306D1 directly addresses the core weakness of this generation. It will include new crankshaft bearings, a refreshed oil pump, and thoroughly flushed oil coolers. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a Discovery 4 or Range Rover Sport without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned 306D1 options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing early signs of bearing wear, or if the engine has already suffered minor bottom-end damage. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new bearings, and a complete overhaul of the valvetrain and oiling system to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom 306D1 rebuild

With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £6,500, the replacement-to-value ratio frequently hits the 🔴 Scrap Threshold for lower-value Discovery 4 examples. items.question: What is the most common failure on the 306D1?
items.answer: The dominant failure pattern on the 306D1 is catastrophic crankshaft bearing failure due to tin-aluminium coating fatigue. This often presents as a distinct cold-start knock before sudden loss of oil pressure. Debris from the failing bearings can circulate, contaminating the turbochargers and oil pump. Once bearing damage occurs, a full 306D1 engine replacement or comprehensive bottom-end rebuild is the only viable solution.

items.answer: The 3.0L 306D1 diesel was fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 4 (L319) and Range Rover Sport (L494) between 2012 and 2016. It is mechanically identical to the broader 306DT family, sharing the same vulnerability to bearing fatigue. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 306D1 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 306D1 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the catastrophic nature of the known bearing failure. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting advanced bearing wear that could fail at any moment. Proper reconditioning proactively replaces the crankshaft bearings with upgraded materials and flushes the oil system. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 306D1 and not the older 276DT or newer 30DDTX?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the oil filter housing. The 306D1 is a 3.0L twin-turbo V6, visually distinct from the older 2.7L V6. It is commonly confused with the newer 30DDTX, which features revised internal components to address the bearing weakness. Fitting the wrong revision or ignoring the specific service history of a 306D1 can lead to rapid repeat failure.
